listed_sector_signals.signal: Japan's Energy Conservation Law benchmark business lines explicitly name several continuous-flow heavy industries (steel, cement, paper manufacturing, petroleum refining, chemical) as regulated benchmark sectors
listed_sector_signals.quote:
Currently set business lines: Iron and steel, electric power, 
cement, paper manufacturing, petroleum refining and chemical.
listed_sector_signals.sector: steel / cement / pulp & paper / petroleum refining / petrochemicals

listed_sector_signals.signal: Sweden's PFE program discussion lists refineries, chemical and steel companies as energy-intensive industry participants (or non-participants due to existing tax exemption)
listed_sector_signals.quote:
Companies that are not participating in the PFE include a large number 
of small and medium enterprises (SME), refineries, and some chemical 
and steel companies (which already have a tax exemption for energy)

listed_sector_signals.signal: Cited reference on energy management in the Swedish pulp and paper industry
listed_sector_signals.quote:
“Exploring energy management in the Swed-
ish pulp and paper industry” Paper presented at the eceee 2009 Summer Study

one_line: The paper compares three national government programs (mandatory in Japan, tax-incentive in Sweden, market-based certification in the US) for accelerating industrial uptake of ISO 50001 energy management systems; continuous-flow sectors like steel, cement, paper, and refining appear only as illustrative regulated/energy-intensive industries, not as an application context.
